text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani arrived in Turkey with a delegation of 240.
- The Islamist-led government gave a 72 percent pay rise to military staff.
- Armed forces deny they are planning their fourth coup in Turkey's modern history and say it is now time for civilian powers to resolve problems.
- Turkey turns to the east with closer ties to Iran. A bilateral defence deal is on the agenda during Rafsanjani's visit to Turkey.

- Women are caught in the trap of ruthless tradition in the southeastern town of Sanliurfa, where they are killed for "tainting the honour" of their families. There have been four honour killings in three years.
- Turkey will begin a programme to sell-off state-owned housing despite a constitutional court decision to annul a law enabling the sale of state property.

- A Germany-based member of the Bucak tribe -- armed by the state in the fight against rebel Kurds -- says the tribe could turn against its paymasters if there were any adverse developments following a scandal linking it to organised crime.
- The Istanbul bar association appoints a commission to investigate a security scandal over alleged ties of the state, police and organised crime.
